articles.title: Predicting the NBA's Top 5 MVP Candidates In 5 Years
articles.summary: The days of LeBron James, Stephen Curry, and Kevin Durant winning MVP trophies are behind us. Flash forward five years, and even the likes of Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Luka Doncic will likely have aged out of the MVP race.
articles.body:
The days of LeBron James, Stephen Curry, and Kevin Durant winning MVP trophies are behind us. Flash forward five years, and even the likes of Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Luka Doncic will likely have aged out of the MVP race.

The NBA is rapidly changing, and the old guard is slowly aging out, while a new crop of young talent has risen to take their spots.

Two quick caveats while predicting the field:

Let's assume good health for everyone on this list.

No players from the current rookie class qualify before seeing them in action.

Here is a look at five potential MVP candidates, five years down the road.

This one is fairly obvious. The NBA needs to be ready for Wembanyama to contend for MVP over the next eight to ten years. He just finished third in MVP voting this past season in his third campaign, was the unanimous Defensive Player of the Year, and is only scratching the surface of just how good he is going to be.

Looking back at last season's numbers, Wembanyama was a force on both ends of the floor. He averaged 25 points on 51.2/34.9/82.7 percent shooting splits while grabbing 11.5 rebounds and swatting away 3.1 shots per game. The Spurs had a 17 net rating while he was on the floor. He led these young Spurs to the Finals in his first postseason.

What the rest of the NBA should be concerned about is that Wembanyama is only 22 years old and just getting started. He hasn't even found his consistent spot on the floor where he can operate and dominate, like Dirk Nowitzki would work the high post.

In a few years, the NBA world may be looking at Wembanyama as the best player on the planet.

The No. 1 pick in the 2020 NBA Draft, Anthony Edwards has lived up to the hype. He already has big moments under his belt in both the regular season and the playoffs. In six seasons, Edwards has made two All-NBA teams, two Western Conference Finals, and has led the Timberwolves back to relevance.

Since Edwards' rookie season, his game has grown exponentially. First look at his three-point percentage: As a rookie, he shot 32.9 percent , and last season, he connected at a 39.9 percent clip. He evolved as a scorer into a legitimate playmaker for his teammates, even though his assist numbers have dipped the last two seasons from his career high of 5.1 assists in the 23-24 season.

The dip has more to do with teams playing more aggressively in their doubles on Edwards, which leads him to give up the ball early in possessions. With LaMelo Ball as his teammate, teams will not be able to double him as immediately as before.

Edwards is a multi-tool player, operating as a playmaker, a three-level scorer, and a post scorer. On top of all that, he's an elite defender.

A season is coming when it all comes together. Five years from now, Edwards will be turning 30 and at the peak of his powers.

It was just two seasons ago that Cade Cunningham finally broke out for the Detroit Pistons. There were flashes along the way, but Cunningham has been able to put it all together and just finished fifth in the MVP vote this past season.

Two seasons ago, Cunningham averaged a career-high 26.1 points; last season, his scoring dipped slightly, but he averaged 9.9 assists a night.

Cunningham is coming into his own as a do-it-all ball player. He has been everything for the Pistons, as they went from a great turnaround story to last year's 60-win team. He cranked up his scoring during the last playoff, aided by shooting 40.2 percent from three on 7.3 attempts.

That type of shooting is what Cunningham needs to bring with him to the regular season. He's a career 34 percent three-point shooter, and that will need to climb. Doing all this while maintaining a nearly double-digit assist average should put him in a position to be an MVP candidate, and five years from now, he will be right in his prime years.

Coming off winning Rookie of the Year, Cooper Flagg in five years' time might be a true force for the NBA world to have to deal with. He'll be just 24 years old and just entering his prime. That should put him squarely in the range of being an MVP contender.

The last 15 games of Flagg's rookie season should be used as the blueprint for ascent. During that stretch, he averaged 24.7 points , 6.8 rebounds, and 5.3 assists while coming up with 1.5 steals and 1.1 blocks per night. That is two-way excellence that also creates opportunities for his teammates. He has all the tools to be a multifaceted player who can lead a franchise.

Of course, after one season, there are areas that need work. He shot just 29.5 percent from three on 3.5 attempts for the year. The mechanics of his shot, though, are fine, and at Duke, he shot 38.5 percent from three.

Flagg should be a better three-point shooter going forward than he was in his rookie season. It should make his play even more deadly going forward.

This is a long-shot bid, but stay with me as I present my case.

Dylan Harper's numbers from his rookie season are not eye-popping: 11.8 points , 3.9 assists, 3.4 rebounds on 50.5/34.3/75.6 shooting splits in just 22.6 minutes a game off the bench.

The numbers don't dazzle, but Harper's game does.

With a litany of guards in San Antonio, Harper came off the bench last season but provided the Spurs with an all-important punch. He gets to the rim at ease, and, more impressively, he was able to do it in the playoffs against some of the toughest perimeter defenders in the NBA right now. He was the best Spurs guard in the Finals; he averaged 18 points and 6.4 rebounds per game; and he did not shrink under the spotlight.

The elephant in the room, of course, is that Harper is teammates with Wembanyama. That will make it more difficult for him to get votes.

Teammates both getting recognized as potential MVPs, has that ever happened? Inde ed, it has. Russell Westbrook and Kevin Durant finished fourth and fifth in MVP voting for the 2015-16 season.

That said, there is still a lot that has to go right for Harper in the next five seasons. Obviously, he needs to be a starter. If that isn't happening by the 2030-31 season, something has gone seriously wrong.

After that, he needs to keep improving his game, especially his three-point shooting.

Harper has the chance to be a truly special player, is already a key contributor on an NBA Finals team, and his role will only grow as he develops.

That growth might put him into MVP contention five seasons from now when he enters his prime.

Mo Dakhil spent six years with the Los Angeles Clippers and two years with the San Antonio Spurs as a video coordinator, as well as three years with the Australian men's national team. Follow him on X, @MoDakhil_NBA .

articles.title: Brazdeikis arranca con el Unicaja a puntazo limpio
articles.standfirst: El lituano aterriza con aura en el Martín Carpena
articles.summary: El lituano aterriza con aura en el Martín Carpena
articles.body: Dos partidos de pretemporada han servido para que Ignas Brazdeikis se convierta en uno de los primeros nombres propios del nuevo Unicaja de Txus Vidorreta. El lituano ha aprovechado sus primeras oportunidades para dejar muy buenas sensaciones y empezar a justificar la apuesta del club malagueño. Ante Melilla firmó 20 puntos, seis rebotes y tres asistencias para 27 de valoración. Su siguiente actuación, en la final de la Copa Andalucía frente al Caja 87 Sevilla, confirmó el buen momento: 15 puntos, ocho rebotes, 18 de valoración y el premio de MVP del encuentro. Más allá de los números, Brazdeikis está demostrando personalidad y protagonismo en ataque. Su llegada a Málaga no generó demasiado ruido, pero su experiencia en la NBA, el Zalgiris o el Olympiacos hacía pensar que podía ser un jugador importante si recuperaba su mejor nivel. Todavía es pronto y los rivales tampoco permiten sacar conclusiones definitivas. La próxima semana, ante La Laguna Tenerife y el Real Madrid en el Torneo Costa del Sol, llegará una prueba mucho más seria. De momento, Brazdeikis ya se ha ganado ser una de las sensaciones del arranque de pretemporada.

articles.summary: Caitlin Clark closed out the group phase of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on a relative high as the United States sailed past Czechia.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark closed out the group phase of the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on a relative high as the United States sailed past Czechia.

Through three games in the tournament, Clark is Team USA's leader in assists and fifth in scoring while playing more minutes than anybody else.

USA's next World Cup opponent and game time set

Caitlin Clark sets unwanted personal record in FIBA World Cup

The United States already had a quarterfinal spot secured when it took the floor against Czechia on Monday. That allowed coach Kara Lawson to ease the workload on her starters a bit and utilize her entire bench.

Clark wound up playing 22 minutes, scoring nine points and dishing out seven assists.

The Indiana Fever guard has been solid in her first major tournament for the senior national team. She opened with a double-double but has since leveled off a bit.

The regression was to be expected. The international game presents a different test to what WNBA players are familiar with, and it's tough for any one star to stand out on a team with as much talent as the United States.

Nobody expected the U.S. to have as much trouble as it did against Italy, so Hungary shouldn't be overlooked. The Hungarians are 19th in the FIBA ranking , though, and got blown out by 46 points against France in the group phase.

Assuming the United States advances, a matchup with Spain or Australia could await. Spain has already punched its ticket to the last eight, with Australia playing Italy on Wednesday.

articles.title: Antetokounmpo ya tiene hogar en Miami: una mansión de 13,5 millones de dólares
articles.standfirst: Tiene un terreno de una hectárea, 1.100 metros cuadrados construidos, ocho dormitorios, 10 baños...
articles.summary: Tiene un terreno de una hectárea, 1.100 metros cuadrados construidos, ocho dormitorios, 10 baños...
articles.body: La llegada de Giannis Antetokounmpo a los Heat ha sido una de las grandes operaciones del mercado NBA. El alero, tras estar toda su carrera NBA en Milwaukee, comenzará una nueva vida en Miami y ya tiene vivienda. No una cualquiera, sino una mansión por la que ha pagado 13,5 millones de dólares. El nuevo hogar de la estrella griega se encuentra en el exclusivo vecindario de Pinecrest, donde suelen residir otros jugadores de los Heat. Tyler Herro vivía ahí hasta que fue incluido en la operación de Antetokounmpo y puso su casa a la venta. También Jimmy Butler tuvo su hogar en el barrio. La mansión de Antetokounmpo tiene unos 1.100 metros cuadrados construidos y cuenta con ocho dormitorios, 10 baños completos, dos aseos, una sala multimedia, piscina, jacuzzi y una casa de huéspedes. El terreno en el que está construida es de cerca de una hectárea y lo único de lo que no dispone es de acceso directo al mar. Es la cuarta propiedad que el jugador griego compra en lo que va de año, pero la única en la que va a residir. Previamente había adquirido inmuebles multifamiliares en Wisconsin, Chicago y Brooklyn por valor de 69 millones de dólares. Con esa última y en mitad del ruido sobre su salida de los Bucks, los aficionados de los Nets y los Knicks llegaron a ilusionarse con su llegada, aunque sólo se trataba de inversiones.

articles.title: WNBA Fans Have A Field Day As Fever Rookie Johnson Interviews Herself
articles.summary: Raven Johnson’s self-interview is a masterclass in controlling your own narrative.
articles.body:
Who said rookies can't be media savvy? Because Indiana Fever 's Raven Johnson just proved everyone wrong when she recently took over her own media session after a team practice. And fans are absolutely loving it!

It's been all about Team USA stars Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston ever since the WNBA season paused for the 2026 FIBA World Cup. As the duo prepares to take on Hungary in Berlin, Germany, in the quarterfinals, the Fever stars have already returned to practice. Rookie Johnson felt this was her time to shine.

Johnson, who was made available to the media after Tuesday's practice, gave the press a crash course by guessing what their questions for her might be! When asked (jokingly) whether she wanted to suggest what reporters should ask her, she used the opportunity to interview herself, asking a few questions about her week off (she traveled to Seattle ) and the current World Cup.

The Fever rookie kicked off her self-interview with the first question: "Raven, how do you feel coming back from the break and working out?"

Answering her own question about returning from the WNBA break, Johnson cheekily said, "Oh, we've been back, guys. We've been in the gym for three days, and everybody looks locked in and ready to make a good playoff run."

The 23-year-old rookie guard fired off another question to herself: "Raven, have you been watching the FIBA Cup, Caitlin and Aliyah?"

"Yes, I've been watching it. Shout out to my girls. They're killing it. And they're definitely going to walk away with the gold medal," Johnson answered again to herself.

Clearly having fun by taking control of her own media session, Johnson posed her third question: "Raven, why are you always smiling?"

The five-foot-nine guard finished her quick-fire round with a big grin across her face, adding, "I'm smiling because I love it here and I'm always smiling because that's just who I am."

As much as the bit cracked every reporter in the room, it looks like fans online loved Johnson's nonchalant attitude through and through.

Responding to the clip shared by an Indianapolis-based sports reporter on X (formerly Twitter), a fan wrote, "Hope you guys gave her your salary for the day. One woman show right there."

Applauding the University of South Carolina graduate for her effort, another fan quipped, "Columbia local media has trained her so well 😂"

A third fan summarized the whole scene, writing, "Raven really said, "I got this one" 😭."

A fourth user also joked, "Since ABC left for FIBA Raven Johnson has taken control of the media and established a dictatorship of the proletariat in Indiana generational run."

Indiana chose Johnson with the 10th overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. She has a stellar reputation as a defensive player and a history of college championships.

Although she made a good impression throughout preseason and training camp, she is still getting used to the professional ranks. As veteran Ty Harris settled into the team and recovered fully from the injury she sustained the season before, Johnson slipped out of the rotation. She is averaging 10.3 minutes, 3.1 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists per game.

Johnson finds herself struggling with shooting, as she only makes 40 percent of her shots from the field and 24 percent of her three-pointers. She is only a rookie, of course, but her length and athleticism allow her to affect the game, especially on defense.

Although Johnson's talent is highly regarded by the Indiana coaching staff, her professional growth is still in its infancy. In her rookie season, Johnson is "comfortable" with where she is now. She continues to pick things up "really fast" and is "off the rip now."

articles.title: Malik Beasley Makes Unusual Travel Request Amid Federal Case
articles.summary: Malik Beasley is trying to keep parts of his normal life moving while his future remains tied to a federal case. The former NBA guard has asked a judge to gi...
articles.body:
Malik Beasley is trying to keep parts of his normal life moving while his future remains tied to a federal case. The former NBA guard has asked a judge to give him more freedom to travel during a brief window in September.

The request comes as Beasley faces strict conditions following his arrest. What makes it unusual is where he wants to go and why.

Malik Beasley Wants To Travel For Family And Work

According to court documents obtained by TMZ Sports , Beasley asked for permission to travel from September 6 through September 15. His proposed stops include Rancho Mirage and Beverly Hills in California, before a work trip to Hawaii.

The California portion is personal. Beasley wants to spend time with his two young children before they return to school, while the Hawaii portion involves a resort promotion connected to his social media work.

His legal team also offered several safeguards as part of the request. Beasley would provide his full itinerary, remain reachable by phone and return to Miami after the trip, according to the filing. Prosecutors do not oppose the request.

That does not mean the court has approved the trip. The request covers a period that began September 6, so the timing could also leave part of the proposed travel window unresolved.

Malik Beasley Remains Under Tight Court Restrictions

The request arrives only months after federal prosecutors charged Beasley in a case involving alleged manipulation of NBA performances for betting purposes. The Justice Department says Beasley and five others were charged in June over an alleged scheme involving sports bribery, illegal betting and money laundering.

Prosecutors allege that Beasley agreed to manipulate his performance in NBA games and provided information that could help others place bets. The government has described the conduct as an effort to turn his NBA performance into a source of illegal betting profit.

An FBI official summarized the allegation in blunt terms, saying Beasley "allowed himself to be bought." The statement reflects the government's accusation, not a finding of guilt.

Beasley has denied the allegations through his legal defense and pleaded not guilty in July. He was released on a $100,000 bond, with conditions that include restrictions related to gambling and contact with people connected to the case.

The Hawaii trip matters because it shows Beasley is trying to keep working while his case plays out. His lawyer said that he has a job on social media. This gives him a clear reason to travel for work, not just for personal reasons.

This creates a tricky situation for Beasley. With his basketball career paused, his travel limited, and a legal battle looming, he's just trying to balance his court-ordered restrictions with his desire to stay connected to his family and keep working.

For now, Beasley's request is only a request. The federal case continues, and any travel approval would come with the restrictions already attached to his release.

articles.title: “You Were Gutless” – Former Indiana Coach Slams Cathy Engelbert After Retirement Announcement
articles.summary: Cathy Engelbert’s retirement announcement has stirred up the WNBA world. As the league begins its search for a new leader, experts are slamming her over mult...
articles.body:
Cathy Engelbert 's retirement announcement has stirred up the WNBA world. As the league begins its search for a new leader, experts are slamming her over multiple controversies. The most recent addition is the former Indiana University Hoosiers interim head coach Dan Dakich.

In a recent YouTube video , Dakich discussed Engelbert's retirement announcement and comments from NBA Commissioner Adam Silver.

Adam Silver praised Engelbert's contributions to the league in his statement. The NBA commissioner said that the 61-year-old was part of the "most significant period of growth in the league's 30-year history." However, Dakich disagreed with Silver's assessment.

"I'll give you two words, Caitlin Clark . That's it. Ain't no more. You held the league back, lady. You were gutless. You've made that league a laughing stock," Dakich said.

The former Indiana University Hoosiers interim coach bluntly described Engelbert as "the worst commissioner in the history of professional sports." Dakich criticized Engelbert's stance on transgender athletes in women's sports.

"See, the W in WNBA stands for women. But Cathy Engelbert and her ilk [kind] can't actually define what a woman is. And that's a problem that ultimately caught up to her hate," Dakich said.

Slamming her further, Dakich added, "Are you nuts, lady? You're 61 years old, and you can't define what a woman is publicly because you're a coward. You are gutless. You are spineless. And now you are out."

Dan Dakich Believes Cathy Engelbert Was Unable To Handle Caitlin Clark

Clark's rise in basketball has been nothing short of astounding. The 2024 NCAA women's championship game featuring Clark drew more viewers than the men's final. When she entered the WNBA, the league's revenue model scaled up, while merchandise sales increased by 200% and the league garnered multi-million-dollar broadcast audiences.

Despite Caitlin Clark 's impact on the league, many experts believe Engelbert failed to advocate for her. Criticizing the WNBA commissioner, Dakich said

"Her retirement comes years after mounting controversies. Her inability to stand up for the golden goose, Caitlin Clark. It's been nothing but a train wreck. Players have mauled Clark out of jealousy. Fans ejected from games over well-later-disproven racist comments, which has been all b-lls–-t."

Cathy Engelbert will retire as WNBA commissioner at the end of this year, on December 31, 2026. Notably, reports have circulated that potential candidates are being shortlisted , and the search process could begin later this month.

articles.title: 76ers sign ex-Knicks $5M 2-time NBA champion to potentially team with LeBron James, Jaylen Brown
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers made an under the radar signing on Tuesday. The back-to-back NBA champion will have to play alongside LeBron James and the rest of the...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have struck gold this offseason, as they have quickly become one of the favorites to win the NBA championship. No one expected the offseason to go this way for Philadelphia after the team was eliminated in the second round of the playoffs last season.

However, it all started with a surprising move for Jaylen Brown . Brown's relationship with the Boston Celtics had reached a breaking point, allowing the 76ers to acquire the former NBA Finals MVP.

"Jaylen Brown has a new home, as the Boston Celtics agreed to send the former NBA Finals MVP to the Philadelphia 76ers in a blockbuster trade Wednesday, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The 76ers are sending Paul George , two first-round picks (2028, 2031) and two second-round selections (2028, 2030) to Boston to complete the deal, sources said," ESPN wrote.

The trade would then get the attention of four-time NBA champion LeBron James . The former MVP ultimately signed with Philadelphia, giving the 76ers another superstar to add to their championship-caliber roster.

"LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers for his final run at another NBA championship, he announced Friday," ESPN's Dave McMenamin wrote. "James, 41, is signing a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania."

The organization has also been making some smaller moves by signing players to Exhibit 10 contracts. On Tuesday, Philadelphia signed back-to-back NBA champion Dillon Jones to an Exhibit 10 contract.

"Back-to-back champ Dillon Jones signed with the 76ers to an Exhibit 10 contract, a team source told ESPN. He'll be a part of Philly's training camp later this month," ESPN's Dave McMenamin wrote.

Jones was selected in the first round of the 2024 NBA Draft by the Washington Wizards before his draft rights were sent to the Oklahoma City Thunder . He spent his rookie season with the Thunder and later joined the New York Knicks on a two-way contract.

The former first-rounder has made $5 million in his career. Jones has already won two NBA championships in his young career, doing so with the Thunder and Knicks in consecutive seasons. Now, he has another opportunity to join a championship contender in Philadelphia. If Jones can earn a two-way contract with the 76ers, he would legitimately have a chance to become an NBA champion in three consecutive seasons.
